method: 10 parallel research agents (one per category) produced a first-pass dataset of all 100 apps via live WebSearch/WebFetch against vendor docs, each app tagged with a confidence level. A human/orchestrator verification pass then independently re-searched a cross-category sample of the highest-leverage claims (official MCP server existence, self-serve access, primary auth method) using fresh WebSearch queries run in the same session, and corrected the dataset where the two passes disagreed.

checks.note: mcp.stripe.com confirmed official, OAuth or restricted API key.
github/github-mcp-server confirmed official, hosted + local options.
Slack shipped an official MCP server (GA Feb 17 2026, docs.slack.dev/changelog/2026/02/17/slack-mcp). First pass missed the official launch and reported community-only.
shopify.dev confirms free dev stores + custom app API access, no paid plan required.

Official MCP *server* (Zendesk data out to agents) is announced for summer 2026 but not live as of Aug 2026 - only a separate 'MCP client' feature (agents in to Zendesk) has shipped. First pass conflated the two launches. Verdict downgraded from 'buildable today' to 'partial'.
$1 free trial no CC required, official hosted MCP at mcp.dataforseo.com confirmed.
mcp.cloudflare.com confirmed official, OAuth 2.1, self-serve API tokens also available.
Intuit Developer Portal signup confirmed self-serve, auto-enrolled Builder Tier, sandbox + OAuth playground available.

first_pass_accuracy: 6/8 (75%) fully correct on the specific claim checked
post_verification_accuracy: 8/8 (100%) after correcting Slack and Zendesk MCP-status errors
honest_caveat: This is an 8-app spot-check, not a full 100-app hand audit - time-boxed given the assignment's own budget guidance. The two real errors caught (both MCP-status claims going stale within the same year they were researched) point to the single biggest fragility in this kind of dataset: MCP server availability is changing faster than any snapshot can track, so buildability verdicts tied to MCP existence should be treated as time-stamped, not permanent.
